memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Obey what I command you today. I will drive out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites. Be careful not to make a treaty with those who live in the land where you are going, or they will be a snare among you. Break down their altars, smash their sacred stones and cut down their Asherah poles.'" - Exod 34:11-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These are hard commands, and we should read them in their setting. God is giving specific instructions to one nation entering one land at one point in history, to protect them from the idolatry that had already nearly destroyed them at Sinai. This is not a template for how Christians treat their neighbours today.

The New Testament could not be clearer about that. Our struggle is not against flesh and blood (Eph 6:12), and our weapons are not of this world (2 Cor 10:4). Jesus told us to love our neighbours and even our enemies (Matt 5:44). Nothing here licenses hostility toward people of other faiths.

What does carry across is the principle underneath: God knows how easily we absorb what we live beside. "They will be a snare among you." Israel had just proved this — four hundred years near Egyptian bull-worship, and under pressure they built a calf.

We are shaped by what we tolerate. Not what we openly approve — what we quietly allow to sit in the corner of our lives.

Note that the altars were to be broken down, not merely avoided. Paul says the same in a spiritual key: put to death what belongs to our earthly nature (Col 3:5). Half-measures with sin do not work.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What influences are quietly shaping you more than you realise?
2. Is there something you are tolerating that should be removed entirely?
3. How do you stay distinct without becoming unloving toward people?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, show me what I have allowed to sit in the corner of my life. Give me courage to remove it completely, and love toward every person around me. Amen.
